what: A top-down view of black ants (captioned 'Lasius niger workers, 25 °C') on a pale floor, going between a nest hole on the left and a pile of pale granular food (it looks like sugar crystals) on the right. The ants' trail pheromone is shown as a blue haze, and a caption says it is drawn in but invisible in real life.
change: Frame 1 (0:07 ant time, time-lapse x15): 4 ants scattered at random, no blue at all. Frame 2 (2:07): about 12 ants, still spread out, and a few faint isolated blue dots appear between the nest and the food. A couple of ants are at the food. Frame 3 (4:15): the view seems to widen or shift (the nest moves further left, the scale bar gets shorter). Many blue blobs now fill the nest-to-food band, patchy and scattered, with some ants clumped near the nest and a small cluster wandering below the band. Frame 4 (6:22): the blobs join into a clearer, continuous-looking corridor, ants are strung along it in single file, and several crowd onto the food. Frame 5 (8:30): the corridor is smoother and wider and splits into roughly two lanes near the food. A few ants wander off it near the food and at the edges. Frame 6 (10:37): the trail is a single solid band, fattest in the middle, with ants in a line along its lower edge, including a tight group of three near the nest, and a few loners out in the empty space. Frame 7 (12:31): the label switches from time-lapse to 'real time' and the camera zooms in (the scale bar gets longer, the nest goes off-screen left). Ants are larger and walk in a procession along the blue band toward and away from the food. Frame 8 (12:39): a further close-up of about 6 ants on the broad blue trail, with one ant at the pile. Over the film: the ant count rises, the blue goes from nothing to dots to a continuous road, the ants go from scattered wandering to lined up, and the camera ends on a tight close-up. I can't tell whether the food pile shrinks. It looks about the same size throughout, apart from the zoom.
where: The strip between the dark nest hole (left) and the pale food pile (right), where the blue trail forms. Early on, look at the first blue dots in the middle. Later, look at the line of ants walking the trail, and at the end at the ant touching the food pile.
planned_or_emergent: It mostly looks emergent. At the start there's no trail and the ants are placed at random. The blue shows up first as scattered, uneven spots that grow and merge over several minutes, it's lumpy and doubled in places (two lanes in frame 5, a wide belly in frame 6), and ants keep straying off it. That irregularity reads as the product of the ants' own footsteps rather than a drawn path. The planned parts are the set: the nest and food are fixed in place from frame 1, and the camera work (the switch from time-lapse to real time and the zoom at the end) is clearly an editorial choice.
